title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS
blurb: A visitor from another star, crossing the picture in three hours.
story: 3I/ATLAS is only the third object ever seen passing through our Solar System from another star. SPHEREx caught it on 14 December 2025, five days before its closest approach to Earth. The fuzzy blob is the comet's cloud of gas and dust. It crosses the whole picture in 3 hours 20 minutes while the stars stay put. Try Time-lapse to watch it go.

doodles.explain: A fuzzy object with a glow around it that moved 564 arcseconds (91.8 SPHEREx pixels) toward the west in 3.2 hours, about 175 arcseconds per hour, while the stars stayed put. Only bodies inside our Solar System cross the sky that fast: an asteroid, or a comet if it looks fuzzy. This is 3I/ATLAS, a known interstellar comet (JPL Horizons).

spectrum.hint: From 1.22 to 1.58 µm it is about equally bright: no strong colour inside this band. Each point is a separate exposure, taken at a different time.

source: NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images (collections spherex_dr1, spherex_qr3)
